Summary: Phase 0: Foundations and governance
Description: Repository skeleton, decision log, backlog, CI, and the warehouse roles. Nothing is generated or loaded yet; this phase makes every later phase reviewable.

Summary: Create the repository skeleton, Makefile, and docker-compose
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Directory layout matches the agreed structure (generator, ingestion, warehouse, controls, lineage, app, exports, dashboards, evidence, tests, docs).
* `docker compose up -d --wait` starts PostgreSQL 16 and the healthcheck passes.
* All nine schemas exist: raw, staging, intermediate, marts, publish_candidate, reporting, sandbox, audit, evidence.
* `make help` lists every target; unbuilt targets exit non-zero naming the phase that builds them.
* `make venv` creates a Python 3.11 environment and installs the project.

Summary: Write the decision log with ADR-001 to ADR-019
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* docs/DECISIONS.md holds 19 entries using the agreed template.
* Each entry has Context, Options considered (2-3 with trade-offs), Decision, Reasons, Consequences, and How a reviewer can verify it.
* An index table at the top lists ID, date, title, and status.
* The first paragraph of each entry is readable by a finance manager or auditor.
* ADR-011 lists the compensating controls for segregation of duties.
* ADR-015 records each provider's free-tier limits with the date they were checked.
* A test asserts entries are numbered contiguously and every index row has a matching section.

Summary: Write a Jira-importable backlog with acceptance criteria
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* backlog/jira_backlog.csv imports into Jira with no manual column mapping.
* One epic per phase; every story links to its epic.
* Every story carries acceptance criteria in its description.
* A test asserts the CSV parses, keys are unique, and every Epic Link resolves to an epic in the file.

Summary: Add pre-commit hooks and a CI workflow that lints and tests
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* pre-commit runs ruff (lint + format) and sqlfluff on staged files.
* `make lint` and `make test` pass locally.
* ci.yml runs lint and tests on every pull request against Python 3.11.
* CI fails when the PR title does not contain a Jira key matching BTB-<number>.
* CI finishes in under five minutes on the demo profile.

Summary: Document branch protection and the PR self-review checklist
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* docs/branch_protection.md gives click-by-click steps to protect main.
* Required status checks are named explicitly.
* Direct pushes to main are blocked and a linear history is required.
* A PR self-review checklist is included and referenced from the PR template.
* The document states that a second approver is the missing control and how it would be added in production (ADR-011).

Summary: Create warehouse schemas and least-privilege roles
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* warehouse/sql/roles.sql creates loader, transformer, reporter, and auditor roles.
* loader writes raw only and may INSERT but not UPDATE or DELETE on audit.
* transformer reads raw and writes the build schemas.
* reporter reads reporting only.
* auditor reads audit and evidence only.
* Default PUBLIC privileges are revoked on the database and the public schema.
* `make roles` is idempotent: running it twice leaves the same grants and errors on neither run.

Summary: Write the project overview and README
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md explains the problem, who has it, and what the project does about it, without jargon.
* README states plainly that data is synthetic and controls are simulated, SOX-style (ADR-019).
* README has a placeholder block for the four live demo links, filled in Phase 1.
* Every number in the README names the command that reproduces it.
* Repository layout and quickstart are documented and verified on a clean checkout.

Summary: Phase 1: Inventory slice, live from day one
Description: One thin path end to end on a public URL: inventory generation, ingestion, dbt models, one reconciliation, the publish gate, and one live dashboard page.

Summary: Generate inventory master data: materials, suppliers, standard costs
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Deterministic for a given seed: two runs produce byte-identical files.
* Material numbers, groups, and units of measure follow the configured domain.
* Standard costs are per material and effective-dated.
* The demo profile produces the configured volumes.
* Designed so Phase 2 extends it without a rewrite.

Summary: Generate purchase orders, goods receipts, and goods issues
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* PO header and line structure follows SAP-style shapes (ADR-002).
* Every goods receipt references a real PO line.
* Goods issues never exceed available quantity when defects are off.
* Movement types distinguish receipts from issues.
* Document numbers are unique within a year.

Summary: Generate GL inventory postings from goods movements
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Every goods movement produces a GL posting at standard cost.
* Postings carry both posting date and document date.
* With defects off, the inventory subledger total equals the GL inventory account balance per period.
* Postings are USD only, as documented in metric_definitions.md.

Summary: Write a control-totals trailer file beside every extract
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Each extract has a sidecar file with row count and value total.
* The trailer is generated from the data, not asserted independently.
* Format is documented and stable for Phase 2 extracts.
* A test asserts the trailer matches the extract it accompanies.

Summary: Declare per-extract schemas and validate with pandera
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Each extract has a declared schema: column names, dtypes, nullability, and value ranges.
* Validation returns the failing rows rather than only a boolean.
* A schema change that breaks an extract fails a test.
* Each extract's natural key is declared alongside its schema (ADR-017).

Summary: Build the incremental, idempotent loader (staging table + anti-join)
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Each file lands in a per-batch staging table in raw, then inserts via a LEFT JOIN anti-join on the declared natural key (ADR-020).
* Running the loader twice in a row inserts zero rows the second time and reports a non-zero skipped count -- not merely an unchanged row total.
* Rows in file, rows inserted, and rows skipped are recorded separately.
* Staging tables are dropped on both the success and the failure path, so raw does not accumulate litter.
* Loads are chunked so the full profile does not exhaust memory.
* A failed load leaves raw in a consistent state.

Summary: Stamp batch provenance on every landed row
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Every raw row carries _batch_id, _source_file, _file_sha256, and _loaded_at.
* The file hash is computed from file bytes before parsing.
* Batch IDs are unique per run and sortable by time.
* Provenance columns survive into staging and mart models.

Summary: Log rejected rows with a reason instead of dropping them
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Invalid rows are written to a rejects table with the failing rule and the raw row.
* Rejected row counts appear in the audit record for that file.
* A file whose rejects exceed a configured threshold fails the run.
* No row is ever silently discarded.

Summary: Create the append-only audit.pipeline_runs table
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* One row per file per run: run ID, batch ID, git commit SHA, file hash, rows in file, rows loaded, rows rejected, start and end time, status, and the role that ran it.
* UPDATE and DELETE are revoked from every role.
* A trigger raises an exception on any UPDATE or DELETE attempt.
* Tests prove both the revoke and the trigger block a modification attempt.
* A reviewer can join a reported number to the file checksum that produced it in one query.

Summary: Build staging models for the inventory extracts
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* One stg_ model per raw table, with no joins.
* Columns renamed to business names and cast to explicit types.
* Units of measure standardised.
* Deduplication rules are explicit and documented.
* Source IDs and batch IDs are preserved on every row.

Summary: Build fct_goods_movements
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Grain is one row per material document line, declared at the top of its YAML.
* Movement type determines the sign of the quantity.
* Keys are unique and not null, enforced by dbt tests.
* Relationships to material and supplier dimensions are tested.
* Every column is described in YAML.

Summary: Build the inventory balance mart
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Inventory value by material group and period, valued at standard cost.
* A custom dbt test asserts no negative on-hand balance.
* Grain is declared and tested.
* The model carries meta certified: true and owner Finance.

Summary: Reconcile inventory subledger to the GL inventory account
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Compares inventory value from goods movements against the GL inventory account balance, per period.
* Writes run ID, check ID, expected, actual, difference, tolerance, and pass/fail to audit.reconciliation_results.
* Assumptions are documented in metric_definitions.md: posting date rather than document date, USD only, valuation at standard cost.
* Classified critical, so a failure blocks publishing (ADR-010).
* With defects off, the check passes with a zero difference.

Summary: Build the publish gate
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Models build into publish_candidate, never directly into reporting.
* Critical checks run before any swap.
* On success, the candidate is swapped into reporting atomically.
* On failure, reporting keeps the last good dataset and audit.publish_log records the reason.
* The swap takes a lock with a timeout and records a failed publish rather than waiting indefinitely.
* A forced failure leaves the dashboard showing its previous refresh time.

Summary: Deploy the first Streamlit trust console page live
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Shows inventory value by material group, the last successful refresh time, and open data-quality issues.
* Connects to the hosted database through the read-only reporter role only.
* The live URL opens on a phone.
* A header states the data is synthetic and the controls are simulated.
* The hosted free-tier limits recorded in ADR-015 are re-verified before deploying.

Summary: Schedule the nightly pipeline against the hosted database
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* pipeline.yml runs nightly on a cron schedule.
* Credentials come from repository secrets and never appear in logs.
* A failed run blocks the publish and leaves reporting untouched.
* Run outcome is visible in the trust console the next morning.
* The workflow can also be dispatched manually.

Summary: Plant and detect a duplicate goods receipt
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* The defect is injected behind its own config switch.
* The injected records are listed in defects_manifest.json.
* The completeness control detects it and the run fails.
* Publishing is blocked and reporting still holds the previous dataset.
* A test asserts the control caught exactly the planted records.

Summary: Plant and detect a backdated GL posting
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* The defect is injected behind its own config switch.
* The closed-period control detects a posting dated into a closed period.
* Publishing is blocked and the reason is recorded in audit.publish_log.
* A test asserts detection matches the manifest exactly.

Summary: Test idempotency, the append-only audit table, and role permissions
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Two consecutive loader runs add zero rows on the second.
* UPDATE and DELETE on audit.pipeline_runs are refused for every role.
* loader cannot read reporting; reporter cannot read raw or sandbox; auditor cannot read business data.
* Each role's allowed actions are also asserted, not just the denied ones.
* Tests run in CI against a freshly generated dataset.

Summary: Phase 2: All sources and planted defects
Description: Widen the slice to every source system at realistic volume, with all 13 defects behind individual switches and a manifest of every injected record.

Summary: Generate multi-level bills of materials for the rack configurations
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* 4 to 6 rack configurations built from GPU, CPU, DIMM, NVMe, PSU, NIC, and chassis components.
* BOMs are multi-level and acyclic.
* Component quantities per configuration are consistent across runs for a given seed.
* A test asserts no BOM cycles and no orphan components.

Summary: Generate supplier invoices
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Invoices reference PO lines and goods receipts.
* Prices agree with the PO within tolerance when defects are off.
* Invoice dates follow receipt dates.
* Quantities and prices support the three-way match control.

Summary: Generate production orders, component consumption, and confirmations
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Consumption follows the BOM for the ordered configuration.
* Confirmations reference production orders.
* With defects off, confirmed quantities tie to MES final-test passes.
* Order status values come from a declared set.

Summary: Generate unit-level MES events with rework loops
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* One event per serial per step attempt, with station, step, timestamps, pass/fail, and failure code.
* Serials traverse assembly, firmware flash, burn-in, and final test in order.
* Rework loops are bounded by the configured maximum attempts.
* Per-step failure rates match the configuration within sampling tolerance.
* The full profile produces at least 5,000,000 events.

Summary: Generate inbound shipments and advance ship notices
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Shipments carry promised and actual dates, carrier, and quantity shipped.
* ASNs precede their receipts.
* On-time delivery is computable from promised versus actual dates.
* Supplier foreign keys are populated when defects are off.

Summary: Generate the chart of accounts, journal entries, and monthly trial balance
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Journal entries cover goods issues, production variances, and COGS.
* The trial balance balances to zero per period.
* The subledger ties to the GL when defects are off.
* Account numbers and types come from a declared chart of accounts.

Summary: Make the full profile run at target volume
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* 12 months, 300 materials, 40 suppliers, 20,000 PO lines, 8,000 production orders, and 5,000,000+ MES events.
* Generation completes on a laptop and the elapsed time is recorded.
* The demo profile still fits the hosted storage cap.
* Memory use stays bounded: generation and loading are chunked.

Summary: Implement injectors for the remaining eleven defects
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Each of the 13 defects has its own config switch, defaulting to off.
* Each injector records every injected record in the manifest.
* Each defect declares the control expected to catch it and whether that control is preventive or detective.
* With all defects off, the subledger equals the GL and every receipt matches a PO.

Summary: Write defects_manifest.json and prove the generator is deterministic
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* The manifest lists seed, profile, timestamp, per-defect counts, and every injected record's natural key.
* With a fixed seed, two runs produce identical extracts and an identical manifest apart from the timestamp.
* With each defect on, the manifest count matches the configured count exactly.
* A test asserts the registry in code and the switches in config.yaml agree, so the two cannot drift.

Summary: Phase 3: Warehouse model in dbt
Description: `make build` turns raw data into a documented, tested star schema, with a performance tuning study on the full profile.

Summary: Extend the staging layer to every source
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* One stg_ model per raw table, with no joins.
* Units of measure standardised across sources.
* Deduplication rules explicit per model.
* Every model and column described in YAML.

Summary: Build the intermediate layer
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* BOM explosion resolves multi-level BOMs to component requirements.
* Receipt-to-PO matching produces a matched, unmatched, and out-of-tolerance classification.
* Unit genealogy links MES events per serial across steps.
* Running inventory balances are computed per material and period.
* Each model's purpose is documented.

Summary: Build the facts and dimensions
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Facts: fct_goods_movements, fct_purchase_order_lines, fct_production_orders, fct_unit_test_events (one row per serial per step attempt), fct_gl_postings.
* Dimensions: dim_material (SCD Type 2), dim_supplier, dim_work_center, dim_date, dim_rack_configuration.
* Every model declares its grain at the top of its YAML.
* Unique, not-null, relationship, and accepted-values tests pass.
* An as-of join to a Type 2 dimension does not multiply fact rows, asserted by a test.

Summary: Add SCD Type 2 snapshots on material master and standard cost
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Snapshots capture valid_from and valid_to per version.
* A cost change produces a new version rather than an overwrite.
* Point-in-time valuation is reproducible for a past period.
* The snapshot supports the cost-approval control in Phase 4.

Summary: Build the KPI marts
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* First-pass yield, WIP units and cycle time, inventory value and aging, purchase price variance, supplier on-time delivery, standard versus actual cost variance, and COGS.
* Each KPI has a business definition in metric_definitions.md.
* Each certified mart carries meta certified: true and an owner.
* Each KPI has at least one dbt test asserting a business rule.

Summary: Document every model and column so dbt docs is the data dictionary
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Every model has a description; every column has a description.
* `dbt docs generate` produces no missing-description warnings.
* Grain is stated for every fact and dimension.
* A CI check fails when a new model or column lacks a description.

Summary: Run the performance tuning case study on the full profile
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* The slowest mart query is identified and named.
* EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) output is recorded before any change.
* At least two remedies are tried: indexing, partitioning by posting period, or an incremental model.
* After numbers are recorded with the same method, on the same data and machine.
* docs/tuning/ holds the write-up with the commands to reproduce it.
* The chosen fix is logged as a new ADR.

Summary: Phase 4: SOX-style controls and reconciliations
Description: Every certified number is backed by automated checks and generated evidence, organised the way auditors test IT general controls. Simulated, SOX-style only.

Summary: Build the completeness, three-way match, MES-to-ERP, and closed-period controls
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Source-to-raw completeness compares row counts and value totals per extract against the control-totals file.
* Raw-to-mart completeness proves no rows lost or duplicated between layers, checked by key.
* Three-way match agrees PO line, goods receipt, and supplier invoice on quantity and price within tolerance.
* MES-to-ERP compares units passing final test against production order confirmations, per period.
* Closed-period integrity finds any posting dated into a closed period.
* Each writes expected, actual, difference, tolerance, and pass/fail to audit.reconciliation_results.

Summary: Control standard cost changes against approval records
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Every change in the standard cost snapshot is joined to an approval record.
* A change with no approval fails the control.
* The control catches the planted unapproved_standard_cost_change defect exactly.
* Severity and tolerance are recorded in the control matrix.

Summary: Build the source freshness control
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Every extract has an expected refresh window declared in config.
* A source older than its window fails the control.
* A stale source blocks publishing of the metrics it feeds, not the whole dataset where that can be scoped.
* The control catches the planted stale_extract defect.

Summary: Add change-management controls to CI
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* CI runs lint, dbt build with tests, and the reconciliations against a freshly generated dataset on every PR.
* A PR title without a Jira key fails CI.
* CHANGELOG.md is generated from merged PRs.
* An emergency-change path is documented: a hotfix branch with after-the-fact review within one business day.
* The segregation-of-duties limitation is restated where the control is claimed (ADR-011).

Summary: Generate a dated user access review report
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* A script queries Postgres grants and role memberships.
* Output is written to evidence/ with a date and is ready for a reviewer's sign-off.
* The report lists each role, its members, and its object privileges.
* An unexpected grant is visible by diffing against the previous report.

Summary: Generate IPE evidence packs for certified report runs
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* evidence/<run_id>/ holds parameters, query text and its hash, source row counts, control totals, reconciliation results, git SHA, timestamp, and the role that ran it.
* A pack is reproducible from the recorded run metadata.
* A sample pack is committed for reviewers.
* The pack demonstrates completeness and accuracy of report data, which is how auditors test information produced by the entity.

Summary: Write the control matrix
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* docs/control_matrix.csv lists control ID, risk addressed, description, type (preventive or detective), frequency, owner, evidence location, and test procedure.
* Every automated check maps to exactly one row.
* Partially implemented controls say so, with a link to the ADR explaining the gap.
* A test asserts every control ID referenced in code exists in the matrix, and vice versa.

Summary: Run the detection test with all 13 defects on
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* A table shows which control caught each of the 13 defects.
* A defect no control catches gets a new control or an ADR explaining the gap.
* Three issues are written up in docs/dq_issue_log.md with root cause, fix, and prevention.
* The table in the README is generated from an actual run, with the command to reproduce it.

Summary: Phase 5: Lineage
Description: Anyone can trace a dashboard number back to the exact source columns that produced it, and CI fails if that trace breaks.

Summary: Publish dbt docs to GitHub Pages on every merge
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* docs.yml generates dbt docs and deploys to GitHub Pages on merge to main.
* The published URL is linked from the README as a live demo link.
* The deployment uses a custom Actions workflow, so the Pages build-rate limit does not apply.
* The site shows the model-level lineage graph.

Summary: Generate column-level KPI lineage with sqlglot
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* sqlglot runs over dbt's compiled SQL, not over hand-written documentation.
* lineage/kpi_lineage.json and a readable lineage/kpi_lineage.md are produced.
* The table lists KPI, mart column, intermediate columns, source system, source table, and source column.
* `make lineage` reproduces both files.

Summary: Extend lineage from source file to dashboard field
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Source file to raw table is resolved using audit.pipeline_runs.
* Reporting column to dashboard field is documented per certified KPI.
* The full path is written up in docs/architecture.md.
* A reviewer can follow one KPI end to end without reading code.

Summary: Tag certified models and drive the lineage report from the tags
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Certified dbt models carry meta: {certified: true, owner: Finance}.
* The lineage report covers exactly the tagged models.
* Adding a certified model automatically brings it into scope.
* A certified model with no owner fails a test.

Summary: Add a CI test that fails when certified lineage cannot be resolved
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* A certified KPI column that cannot be traced to raw source columns fails CI.
* The failure message names the KPI and the unresolved column.
* The test is part of the required status checks on main.
* Lineage therefore cannot break silently.

Summary: Phase 6: BI dashboard, trust console, and failure demo
Description: One dashboard leaders could actually use, where every number shows whether it can be trusted, plus a safe, repeatable failure demonstration.

Summary: Build the Tableau dashboard pages
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Confirm first whether a Windows machine is available and record the answer as an amendment to ADR-012.
* Operations page: yield, WIP, cycle time by work center.
* Inventory page: value, aging, negative-balance exceptions.
* Procurement page: purchase price variance, supplier on-time delivery.
* Cost page: standard versus actual variance, COGS.
* Built from the exported certified datasets, not from a live connection.
* Every page footer shows the batch ID and extract timestamp it was built from, and states the data is synthetic.
* On Windows, the same pages are rebuilt in Power BI Desktop and the .pbix is committed.

Summary: Build mart_kpi_trust_status
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Per KPI: last successful refresh time and whether its reconciliations passed in that run.
* Built on the audit tables.
* Drives the trust indicator on every KPI tile.
* A KPI whose reconciliation failed is visibly untrusted rather than merely stale.

Summary: Build the Streamlit trust console pages
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Pages: Inventory, Production completion, Supplier delivery, Data-quality issues, Pipeline runs and reconciliations, Lineage lookup, and Evidence.
* Lineage lookup lets a user pick a KPI and see its source columns.
* Evidence page offers a sample evidence pack for download.
* Connects only through the reporter role against certified reporting tables.
* A production/sandbox toggle switches which schema is displayed.

Summary: Export certified datasets with a manifest
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* `make export` writes certified reporting tables to exports/ as CSV and Parquet.
* A manifest records batch ID, row counts, checksums, and refresh time.
* Only data that passed the publish gate is exported.
* The manifest states that the data is synthetic.
* A test asserts manifest checksums match the exported files.

Summary: Build the manual failure demo workflow
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* demo_failure.yml is a manual workflow with a defect picker.
* It runs against the sandbox schema only.
* The console toggle shows the blocked publish and the retained last good dataset.
* Live reporting data is provably never touched, asserted by a test.
* The workflow completes in under five minutes so it can be run during a demo.

Summary: Capture dashboard screenshots for the README
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* A screenshot per Tableau page is committed to dashboards/.
* Screenshots are dated.
* The README embeds them so a reviewer need not open the workbook.
* A three-minute screen recording is linked as the backup plan.

Summary: Phase 7: Documentation, demo script, and definition of done
Description: A hiring manager understands the project in two minutes, an engineer can rebuild it in ten, and it can be demonstrated live in five.

Summary: Write metric definitions and resolve the shipped-versus-complete conflict
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Every certified KPI has a business definition in finance and operations language.
* The deliberate conflict is written up: ERP counts a unit shipped at goods issue, MES counts it complete at final test.
* Both views, the month-end impact, and the chosen definition are documented.
* The choice is recorded as a new ADR.
* Each definition names the model and column that implements it.

Summary: Write the architecture document with a diagram
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* A diagram shows sources, ingestion, warehouse, publish gate, exports, and dashboards.
* The end-to-end lineage path is drawn and described.
* Schema purposes and the role model are documented.
* The diagram is committed in a format that renders on GitHub.

Summary: Write the README with live links and reproducible numbers
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* The four live demo links are at the top: trust console, Tableau dashboard, dbt docs, and the repository.
* Then: the problem, how to run it, the defect-detection results table, the tuning before-and-after numbers, and a Jira board screenshot.
* Links to DECISIONS.md, the control matrix, the lineage report, and a sample evidence pack.
* It states plainly that the data is synthetic and the controls are simulated.
* Every number names the command that reproduces it, and a test asserts no number appears without one.

Summary: Write the five-minute demo script
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Seven steps at roughly 45 seconds each, matching the agreed running order.
* The backup plan is included: warm up every live link five minutes beforehand, with a screen recording and dated screenshots as fallback.
* The failure demo step runs against sandbox only.
* The script has been rehearsed end to end and the elapsed time recorded.

Summary: Write interview notes with answers drawn from the decision log
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* Ten likely questions covering ITGC areas, IPE, preventive versus detective controls, SCD Type 2, grain, and lineage.
* Each answer cites the ADR or control it comes from.
* Answers state limitations honestly, including segregation of duties.
* No answer claims SOX compliance.

Summary: Verify the definition of done on a clean machine
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* `make all` rebuilds data, warehouse, controls, lineage, exports, and evidence from scratch on a clean checkout.
* All live links work from a fresh browser and the nightly run updates the refresh time.
* The failure demo blocks publishing in sandbox and leaves the live demo untouched.
* CI is green, every merged PR carries a Jira key, and the backlog CSV imports into Jira cleanly.
* All 13 planted defects are detected, or the gap is documented in DECISIONS.md.
* Every certified KPI has a definition, end-to-end lineage, and at least one reconciliation.
* DECISIONS.md has an ADR for every tool, model shape, metric definition, and control design.
* Every number in the README matches a reproducible run.

Summary: Distinguish a source-side duplicate from an already-loaded row
Description:
Acceptance criteria:
* A duplicate on the natural key *within a single extract* is rejected and reported, not silently skipped -- it means the upstream interface posted twice.
* A row already present in raw from an earlier run is skipped and counted, not rejected -- it means the pipeline was rerun.
* The two counts are recorded separately in audit.pipeline_runs.
* A test asserts a rerun produces skips and zero rejects, and that a planted within-file duplicate produces rejects matching defects_manifest.json exactly.
* Without this distinction the duplicate_goods_receipt control cannot fire, so CTRL-001 depends on it.
